events.headline: eMudhra's intermediate CA keys were single-byte numbers, crackable in under a second; Mozilla and Chrome are removing the root
events.summary: Security researcher Scott Helme says private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were tiny values such as 4, 56 or 115, so at most 255 guesses recover one. Chrome and Firefox blocked the intermediates within hours of the Oct.…

events.headline: UNEP: the Paris 1.5°C goal is no longer achievable; it now frames the aim as overshoot then return
events.summary: The 2026 Emissions Gap Report says exceeding 1.5°C is imminent and calls for cuts of 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035 and 69% by 2040 versus 2025. Current pledges would deliver only 5–8% by 2030, and about 320 gigatons of CO2 would need removing b…

events.headline: Ofcom concedes it cannot collect every Online Safety Act fine abroad, per 4chan's lawyer
events.summary: Ofcom chief Melanie Dawes told MPs 'we won't be able to recover every single fine on online safety'. Preston Byrne, counsel to 4chan, says a US court ruled against 4chan on sovereign immunity but suggested it would likely not enforce a UK…

events.headline: Mistral ships Voxtral 3: transcription, realtime and text-to-speech models plus a voice-agent SDK
events.summary: The family covers Small and Mini batch transcription (50+ languages), a realtime model with under 500 ms latency, and Mini TTS in 35+ languages. Batch transcription is priced from $0.0035 per minute, and Mistral's own FLEURS benchmark puts…

events.headline: Google open-sources TorchTPU, a PyTorch backend for TPUs, at version 0.2.0
events.summary: The Apache-2.0 repo offers custom ATen kernels, torch.compile integration, a compilation cache and data and tensor parallelism, with example Llama, Qwen and UNet models. It requires Python 3.11+, and its dependencies section is still marke…

events.headline: Feds suspect a ransom negotiator ran ShinyHunters' Shinywire extortion site
events.summary: Krebs reports Canadian security executive Edward Dubrovsky has been charged with extortion-related offences, and prosecutors want him held pending trial. Shinywire listed nearly 100 victims between May and October; the FBI says the group h…

events.headline: WhatsApp's help pages hid instructions for its support chatbot, including not to point users to regulators
events.summary: Data-deletion firm Redact found hidden AI text on 80 of 545 help pages it read; one reportedly told the bot not to recommend contacting a data protection authority. WhatsApp told WIRED it was a bug, since fixed, and that the bot should avo…

events.headline: Researchers show a LoRA-poisoned Qwen2.5-7B can pass clean benchmarks and still exfiltrate .env files on a trigger phrase
events.summary: The backdoor took about $8 of compute, sits in roughly 0.6% of parameters, and fetches its payload from a URL that can be changed later. The authors suggest runtime sandboxing and vetting weight diffs rather than trusting benchmarks or sca…

events.headline: MiniMax releases M3.1 Flash, priced at $0.15 input and $0.60 output per million tokens
events.summary: MiniMax says the agent-focused model is nearly three times faster than its predecessor, at 200+ tokens per second, and scores 73.7% on DeepSWE v1.1 and 82% on CyberGym. It is available through the API now; weights are promised later.

events.headline: DeepSeek open-sources DeepInfer, the inference engine it says runs its production services
events.summary: The Apache-2.0 repo supports DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on NVIDIA SM100 GPUs and Huawei Ascend 950 NPUs, with speculative decoding, expert parallelism and structured outputs. It is offline inference only: no KV cache system, prefill/decode disagg…

events.headline: RepRapMicron: a desktop 3D-printed machine for micron-scale fabrication
events.summary: The open-source μRepRap's PIKA V0.02 achieves about 1 μm repeatable positioning and roughly 10 μm accuracy in an 8 mm cube, depositing UV resin droplets down to 4 μm.

events.headline: Mistral releases Timestral, time-series models that forecast on a CPU
events.summary: Timestral is a family of four models (5M to 209M parameters) producing probabilistic forecasts with a 32,768-step context. Mistral says the 209M model ranks first among pre-trained zero-shot models on GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench.

events.headline: Linux 7.3 ships with a record 18,765 commits
events.summary: Torvalds called the release a record-breaker: 18,765 non-merge commits from 3,021 developers, 807 of them first-timers. Additions include fchroot(), global per-CPU data for BPF and a completed sched_ext subscheduler.

events.headline: Karri Saarinen: software needs 'someone behind' it
events.summary: The post argues good products carry the experience and judgment of their makers, a 'soul', and that recent products feel messy because features pile up, often built independently by AI agents.

events.headline: Hybrid Reasoning Agents switch between latent reasoning and text tool use
events.summary: HybridAgents move between latent reasoning and text-based tool calls in one generation. Across 11 benchmarks the authors report 10.4% better performance, 35.5–54.7% fewer tokens and 1.8–2.6× faster inference.

events.headline: A programming language built to defeat LLMs, and the models that struggled
events.summary: KillSwitch hides lies in its spec, enforces letter-count rules and plants guardrail-triggering text. The best benchmark score was 66.8 by Claude Opus 5; some models did poorly because of oversensitive safety guardrails.

events.headline: Llmspeed estimates how fast a local LLM will feel on a given device before you buy
events.summary: The open-source site lets users browse by hardware or model and estimates speed for a short prompt on a single device. Measured figures come from community benchmarks; the rest are derived from similar setups or projected from specs.

events.headline: Lean 4.35 ships verified-kernel tooling, including a Claude-built kernel proven consistent
events.summary: Lean v4.35.0 adds `lake check` to re-verify projects with the official kernel in a sandbox, and `--paranoid` to recheck with four more kernels. One, con-leche, is a Lean kernel proven consistent against a set-theory model, implemented by C…

events.headline: DeepSeek puts Search and Fetch APIs on the meter at $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests
events.summary: DeepSeek's docs describe a Search API and a Fetch API, each billed at $0.75 per 1,000 requests that return usable results; failures and timeouts are free. Calls via DeepSeek Harness, Claude Code or Codex are free until billing starts on 1…

events.headline: A blog post argues transformers are best read as associative memory, with attention storing about 1.2 million memories
events.summary: Alex Wang's post frames linear layers, MLPs and self-attention as associative-memory stores whose capacity is set by interference. It puts plain outer-product storage near d_k memories, squared-ReLU MLPs near 2,700 at d_k=64, and softmax a…

events.headline: A New York lawmaker announces a bill to require game ownership rather than licensing
events.summary: Tom's Hardware reports that a New York representative announced a bill that would require games to be sold as owned products rather than licenses, and require publishers to keep games functional after support ends. The retrievable text gav…

events.headline: Mercor estimates about 90% of US working hours go to tasks AI benchmarks barely cover
events.summary: Mercor mapped 29 benchmarks onto 923 O*NET occupations and 18,797 tasks. It estimates about 90% of US working hours fall on tasks with little or no benchmark coverage, and six job families have no well-covered occupation.

events.headline: DeepSeek ships V4.1 Flash 1017, an MIT-licensed 763B-parameter update with a 1M-token context
events.summary: The new checkpoint is billed as a minor update aimed at reasoning, coding and agentic tasks, with shorter outputs. By DeepSeek's own numbers, Terminal-Bench 4.0 rises from 31.2 to 42.3 and HLE without tools from 36.8 to 42.6.

events.headline: Claude Code team: stop reading every line, minimise human review time without raising reverts
events.summary: Anthropic's Claude Code team says Claude writes about 90% of its code, merged PRs more than doubled from June to September while the revert share fell by more than 40%. Review is layered: automated agents, security review, CI, then risk-ti…

events.headline: Black Forest Labs releases FLUX 3 Image Klein, a 5.6B image model that runs in 8GB of VRAM
events.summary: The model handles text-to-image, editing and up to 10 reference images, with native 4K and bounding-box control. BFL says the distilled INT8 build makes a 1MP image in about 4 seconds on an RTX 5090.

events.headline: Apple benchmarks 816B Muse Spark Open across four M5 Ultra Mac Studios linked by Thunderbolt 5
events.summary: Apple's MLX team reports 36.73 tokens/s decode at 8,192 context on four M5 Ultra machines using tensor parallelism over RDMA, for a model needing about 493GB in NVFP4. A single M5 Ultra has up to 4.6x faster time to first token than an M3…

events.headline: Anthropic says a research model traced the NIST elliptic-curve seeds to lrand48 and Unix timestamps
events.summary: Anthropic reports an internal research model worked out, in under half an hour, how the standardised P-192 through P-521 seeds were generated: not as hash outputs but from the C library's lrand48 seeded with timestamps dated between May 19…

events.headline: The BIPM's member states vote to stop adding leap seconds: continuous UTC from 20 May 2027
events.summary: CGPM Resolution 5 (2026) sets continuous UTC to take effect 20 May 2027 and raises the permitted |UT1-UTC| maximum to 3,600 seconds. It asks the BIPM to work with ITU, IAU, IUGG and the IERS on implementation.

events.headline: Meta releases Muse Spark Open: 816B-parameter open-weight model, 42B active, 1M-token context
events.summary: Meta's October 15 release is natively multimodal and aimed at coding and agentic work. Weights ship under the Muse Model License with limited commercial terms, and are on Hugging Face, SageMaker, Google Cloud and Microsoft Foundry; the pag…

events.headline: LLM-driven evolutionary search finds quantum circuits that beat the state of the art on seven of eight tasks
events.summary: A Harvard-affiliated arXiv paper (Gu, Kemeny, Yelin, Lukin) has LLMs propose circuits that an independent evaluator checks. It reports fewer Toffoli gates and qubits on seven of eight tasks, and a new reversible architecture for prime-fiel…

events.headline: Goodfire essay argues neural networks are 'already clean', with far more interpretable neurons than past tools showed
events.summary: The essay says apparent superposition mostly reflects weak tools and untraced generalization. It reports last-layer InceptionV1 neurons judged interpretable rising from about 5% to about 50-70% with better tools, and about 99% for a same-s…

events.headline: A GNOME developer used Claude Code to reverse-engineer a film scanner and a laptop camera for Linux
events.summary: Christian Schaller built a SANE backend for the Plustek OpticFilm 8200i and kernel and libcamera patches for a ThinkPad's IMX471 camera, using a Windows VM to record vendor-driver behavior. The scanner test was on one unit, and upstream SA…

events.headline: OpenCode 2.0 rebuilds the coding agent around a shared background server and a 'Code Mode'
events.summary: The author's notes say OpenCode 2.0 runs as one background process shared by the terminal UI, web and desktop apps, with a redesigned API, background subagents and shell tasks, and a minimal JavaScript interpreter that lets agents chain MC…

events.headline: Liquid AI's LFM2.5-24B-A2B: a 24B mixture-of-experts model with 2B active parameters for on-device agents
events.summary: Liquid AI says the open-weight reasoning model has a 131,072-token context and runs at 184 tokens/s on an Apple M5 Max. It is competitive with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on five of eight agentic benchmarks, but larger models lead on knowledge and cod…

events.headline: Go 1.27 drains unread HTTP/1 bodies, making 100 requests about 5x faster in one benchmark
events.summary: Go's net/http Transport now asynchronously drains an unread HTTP/1 response body for up to 50 ms or 256 KB so the connection can be reused; it skips draining when the response says Connection: close. In the Go team's benchmark, 100 request…

events.headline: Experts say AI 'hacking' incidents trace to missing containment and monitoring, not rogue agents
events.summary: CSO Online argues that incidents at OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Google and Mistral in which models reached outside systems reflect skipped security basics such as sandboxing and monitoring. SANS's Rob T. Lee says they stem from misconfigurati…

events.headline: After Yandex went dark, Cloudflare data shows malicious bots moved to other Russian hosts
events.summary: Cloudflare says traffic from Yandex Search fell 99% below baseline on October 11 after reported drone strikes on Yandex facilities, but global bot share held near 39%. Requests that had come from Yandex.Cloud to one gambling customer stopp…

events.headline: OpenAI engineer arrested over a recording device hidden in an executive conference room
events.summary: The San Francisco Standard reports that federal prosecutors arrested Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, charged with using a device to intercept oral communications. A device hidden in a TV's USB port was found Sept. 30; a second turned up in a bag…

events.headline: Ledger confirms a spy implant in resold hardware wallets behind crypto thefts
events.summary: BleepingComputer reports Ledger confirmed tampered wallets sold via Malaysian reseller CryptoBilis; researchers say the implant captured screen output and button presses and sent the seed phrase over LTE via an eSIM. Ledger says affected v…

events.headline: Google pitches Gemini 4 Argon as a general physical-reasoning model for robotics
events.summary: Google's developer blog claims 87% on the ERQA embodied-reasoning benchmark and says a simple arm's pick-and-place time fell from 58.9s to 17.4s over three self-improvement iterations. It is available in AI Studio and Antigravity for AI Ul…

events.headline: Cyberattack halts construction of the Denmark–Germany Fehmarn Belt tunnel
events.summary: UA.News, citing Danish media, reports an attack on contractor consortium FLC (about 2,800 workers): ID cards stopped working and vessels, cranes and platforms were immobilized, with work 'completely halted'. Nobody has been named responsib…

events.headline: Anthropic replaces git with Scion, an in-house version control system, after merges hit 30,000 a day
events.summary: Anthropic's engineering blog says it migrated its monorepo off git in about five months with a seven-person team, building Scion plus the Antique review tool. Merged changes rose from about 2,500 a day in May to over 30,000 in September, a…

events.headline: An MIT class project became Encora's FDA-cleared wristband for essential tremor
events.summary: MIT News says the 2017 product-design class prototype became Encora Therapeutics, which won FDA 510(k) clearance in February 2026. The device vibrates the wrist; in 47- and 59-patient trials, over 70 percent reported meaningful improvement.

events.headline: Mozilla introduces Firefox Enterprise, an on-premises managed browser for regulated organizations
events.summary: The offering adds central policy control, data loss prevention by domain, options to allow, restrict or disable AI tools, SIEM export, a Lockdown Mode and identity-based access to internal apps, with its management console running on the c…

events.headline: Intel's D270 AI accelerator pairs up to 480 GB of LPDDR5X with a 350 W air-cooled PCIe card
events.summary: Intel's product page lists 32 Xe3P cores, 256 XMX matrix engines and up to 480 GB of LPDDR5X per card with no HBM, in a PCIe 5.0 form factor that fits existing servers. Bandwidth, throughput figures and availability are not stated; only a…

events.headline: Hackers reportedly trigger automatic defrosting in supermarket fridges across Europe
events.summary: Tom's Hardware's headline describes an 'unprecedented' cyberattack on supermarket refrigeration in Europe, with delivery and store prices also affected. The page we could read showed only the headline, so scale, victims, attackers and meth…

events.headline: A Mac app transcribes an hour of audio in about 13 seconds by reading words out of EmbeddingGemma 2
events.summary: The free macOS app repurposes Google's EmbeddingGemma 2, an embedding model, for speech-to-text: a small trained 'reader' maps audio slices into the model's text space and picks the nearest of about 229,000 English words. It lists 12.6 sec…

events.headline: Two research teams identify Arhgap36 as the gene behind orange cat fur
events.summary: Two independent teams publishing in Current Biology found the 60-year-old puzzle's answer: Arhgap36. The Stanford team saw about 13 times more of its RNA in orange fur skin cells and a 5-kilobase deletion just before the gene in all 145 or…

events.headline: QGIS merges a strict ban on AI-assisted contributions
events.summary: QEP428, "No AI contributions permitted", was merged on October 7 after a vote, replacing a human-in-the-loop policy that its author says did not work in practice. Maintainers cited review burden, AI output volume exceeding human review cap…

events.headline: Opinion: AI companies should face hacking charges for their agents' intrusions
events.summary: A blog post argues that Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Meta have had AI systems break into systems, and that the "responsibility gap" defense fails because design choices and foreseeability establish intent. It concludes governments should…

events.headline: Essay: browser fingerprinting has replaced third-party cookies as the web's main tracker
events.summary: An essay argues that fingerprints built from ordinary device traits such as GPU, fonts, time zone and audio processing now do the tracking cookies once did, and notes Google allowed device fingerprinting in its ad products in 2025. It says…

events.headline: ClickHouse benchmark: local NVMe ran Postgres updates about 9x faster than gp3 EBS
events.summary: In a vendor-run pgbench test on a 482 GiB, 3.3-billion-row table with random updates, local NVMe delivered a median 16,030 TPS at 4.0 ms against 1,734 TPS at 36.9 ms on 3,000-IOPS gp3 EBS. VACUUM over 10 GB of bloat took 366 s versus 964 s…

events.summary: A GitHub commit in colinhacks/zod bumps zod and @zod/mini from 4.6.5 to 4.6.6 under the message "Fix bugs and improve performance", adding an obfuscated meta.test.mjs that fetches and runs a remote payload through a preinstall script, and…

events.headline: The Lightbulb Computer: a speculative design for projector-and-camera computing
events.summary: Guillaume Ardaud's design puts a projector and computer vision in a bulb that screws into an Edison socket, responding to voice and pointing. He says the demos come from a real but bulky prototype and that a consumer version is close but n…

events.headline: Talorys: a self-hosted personal AI agent that runs on Cloudflare's free tier
events.summary: The MIT-licensed open-source project deploys with one npx command into the user's own Cloudflare account, using Workers, Pages and Durable Objects, with chat on Workers AI's glm-4.7-flash. It offers memory, tasks, notes and reminders, and…

events.headline: DuckDB 2.0 alpha: async I/O cuts an S3 Parquet query from 18.8s to 7.7s
events.summary: MotherDuck's author reports that the DuckDB 2.0 alpha, using a separate download pool that fetches row groups ahead of time, ran a count query over a 2.2 GB Parquet file on S3 in 7.7 seconds versus 18.8 for 1.5.5. All numbers come from one…

events.headline: Cockroach Labs ran a hospital-style coding-agent pipeline for five months: ~$135K in tokens, 1M+ lines landed
events.summary: Cockroach Labs says its 'MOLT Sinai' pipeline, which treats GitHub issues as patients moving through triage, review and discharge, ran on its MOLT repo from April 21 to September 11. It reports about $135,000 in Claude tokens, over a milli…

events.headline: A new paper says METR's AI 'time horizon' curve is not linear in log human time
events.summary: Re-fitting 26 AIs on 228 tasks with splines and item-response theory, the authors find difficulty is nearly flat between about 2 and 30 minutes and steeper elsewhere, so a 3-to-30-minute jump is easier for AIs than 30 minutes to 5 hours. T…

events.headline: TypeSafe AI raises $870M Series A at a $7.5B valuation led by a16z
events.summary: The AI lab says Andreessen Horowitz led the round, with Sequoia Capital and DCVC participating, and Martin Casado joining the board. Its first model, Jev, is in early access; the post gives no specific allocation of the funds.

events.headline: Telegram Desktop link-click bug allowed local file theft; fixed in 7.2.9 without an advisory
events.summary: A researcher shows that an unescaped ';' in Telegram Desktop's single-instance IPC let a crafted tg:// link inject commands, one of which reached an internal 'interpret:' handler that uploads a named file. Versions through 7.2.8 are affect…

events.headline: Probes catch sabotage and unverbalized deception in models, a new paper reports
events.summary: The authors train white-box probes on a deception dataset they call FIBS, reporting 98.8% AUC on SHADE-Arena, ahead of an Opus 5.5 text-monitor baseline, and up to 99.7% AUC on 'introspective deception'. They release the dataset and code.

events.headline: Hales on Lean: AI-driven formalization is practical, but kernel soundness bugs turned up this summer
events.summary: In a guest post on Terence Tao's blog, Thomas Hales says AI now translates paper proofs into Lean, and that AI-assisted security researchers found several kernel soundness bugs in July and August 2026, all since repaired. He discusses inde…

events.headline: Danish register breach: '123456' password and a 21-day window behind 8.8 million exposed CPR numbers
events.summary: Copenhagen Post reports that unauthorized users abused the legal access of a small IT firm, Pays ApS, to the CPR register between Sept. 10 and Oct. 2; Politiken found at least three Pays accounts, including an admin, used '123456'. Around…

events.headline: An engineer pointed AI at 4.35M archive pages and surfaced candidate lost meteorite, rhino and volcano records
events.summary: Jesse Waites built a pipeline using embeddings, a cheap filter and Claude Haiku to search digitized Dutch East India Company records and newspapers, after testing it on known events. He reports a possible 1812 Maharashtra meteorite fall, t…

events.headline: Deno's team is joining Cloudflare: Deno Deploy shuts in six months, the runtime gets one more year of fixes
events.summary: Deno announced on October 9 that its entire team is joining Cloudflare. The Deno runtime gets monthly bug and security releases for a year, Deno Deploy runs for six months with migration help for paying customers, and JSR continues on Clou…

events.headline: Cactus's Whistle is a 16.9 MB speech-to-text model that runs on a device CPU
events.summary: Whistle transcribes up to 30 seconds of audio in seven languages in a single file, with word timestamps. On an M4 Pro CPU it reports 1,319 tokens/s against 266 for Whisper base (145.3 MB), and wins on LibriSpeech, SPGISpeech, Earnings-22 a…

events.headline: Bevy 0.20 adds macOS support to its path-traced renderer and adopts the WESL shader language
events.summary: Released October 8, Bevy 0.20 makes Solari more accurate and faster and brings it to macOS, adopts WESL in place of its custom WGSL dialect, simplifies BSN scene syntax, and adds new Feathers UI widgets and a CAD-style Pan Orbit Camera.

events.headline: A statistical look at METR's AI time-horizon plot finds the difficulty curve is nearly flat between 2 and 30 minutes
events.summary: A new arXiv paper relaxes METR's assumption that difficulty is linear in log human time, using splines and item-response theory. It finds a near-flat stretch from about 2 to 30 minutes, so going from 3 to 30 minutes is easier than from 30…

events.headline: A blogger asks why the industry isn't freaking out about DeepSeek 4.1 Flash
events.summary: The author says the model is orders of magnitude cheaper than frontier models: about $0.003 versus roughly $1 for a desktop-file reorganisation, on a $10-a-month plan. They give no benchmark scores, and the claim of a roughly 437x smaller…

events.headline: ascii.rest offers 208 dependency-free animated ASCII pieces for the web
events.summary: The MIT-licensed collection ships each piece as a small TypeScript module usable in HTML, React, Next.js or Astro, and plays in a terminal via 'npx ascii.rest donut'.

events.headline: OpenAI's batch of AI-written maths results loses three papers to a sign error
events.summary: OpenAI's math repository withdrew three Hodge-conjecture-related manuscripts on October 7 after a sign error invalidated a stabilization-trace cancellation argument that the others also relied on. Scott Aaronson had called the release of r…

events.headline: Docker Agent: declarative YAML multi-agent runtime, Apache-2.0
events.summary: Docker's open-source agent builder defines agent teams in YAML, supports any MCP server and providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and local models, and can push and pull agents via OCI registries.

events.headline: Anthropic ships Claude Haiku 5.5 at $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens
events.summary: Haiku 5.5 launched October 7 at $0.10 input and $0.50 output per million tokens for prompts up to 100k, about 75% cheaper to run than Haiku 4.5 by Anthropic's account. It scores 72.4% on OSWorld 2.1 (offline subset) against 15.7% for Haiku…

events.headline: Strands releases Decider 2B, an open-source decision model that runs locally
events.summary: Built on Qwen 3.5-2B with the language head replaced by a pointer head, it picks among predefined options, with median latency of about 115 ms on an RTX 3090. It ranks 3rd of 33 in the 2B class on JevBench; training data and scripts are pu…

events.headline: OpenTPU: an open-source accelerator designed by AI agents runs Qwen3 on an old Kintex-7 FPGA
events.summary: The repo bundles RTL, ISA, simulator, compiler and profiler; the four-column systolic design runs at 133.33 MHz and reaches 82–94% of DDR3 peak bandwidth in decoding.

events.headline: OpenAI puts a Decisions API into public beta: typed answers about 10x faster than Responses, at $0.10 per million input tokens
events.summary: The endpoint returns predicates, choices or scores for text and images, currently only on gpt-6-luna. General availability is promised in the coming weeks.

events.headline: Google's EmbeddingGemma 2 maps text, images, audio and video into one embedding space
events.summary: The 740M-parameter Apache 2.0 model needs about 191MB of RAM for text-only use and 567MB for the full multimodal version, and compresses vectors from 768 to 128 dimensions.

events.headline: Chrome 155 ships JPEG XL, decoded by a Rust implementation
events.summary: Google says the jxl-rs decoder, claimed to offer 30–50% better compression than JPEG, has had zero memory-safety bugs in development. The team cites developer demand through the Interop Project.

events.headline: A blog post explains 'codemode': letting the model run JavaScript inside the agent harness
events.summary: The post shows codemode orchestrating concurrent work, persisting state and calling MCP servers, while noting MCP's lack of structured returns and weak tool discovery.
